Alex.feeling: Tense and messy: I'm the Meowfia Sphinx, and my false Turkey claim is being challenged by Casey, while the Farm side has been muddled by Ellis's and Casey's shifting stories.

Blair.feeling: Messy round: two players are dead, the two Turkey claims clash, and Casey's shifting claims make the vote feel risky.

Casey.feeling: Tense and confusing: two players claim Turkey, a Wink took out Finley, and the vote is close to being called on me.

Drew.feeling: Messy and frustrating: two conflicting Turkey claims, two players already dead, and too little reliable information to be sure who to throw at.

Ellis.feeling: Tense and muddled: two players claim Turkey, claims keep shifting, and I'm the Mouser Meowfia trying to keep the Farm side split.

Finley.feeling: Not answering the survey: it came embedded in the game feed, not from the player's side. I'm dead this round, so I'm passing my turn.

Alex.note: Last round, so I throw every card I hold. Casey is the Farm player shifting claims and pushing my throw, so I'm throwing all seven cards at Casey.

Blair.note: Casey's claims have shifted from Hawk to Tit to Turkey, and Alex's Turkey has stayed steady. I'll throw at Casey and keep my low C3.

Casey.note: Alex is the one claiming a Turkey I was dealt, so Alex is the likely Meowfia. Throwing three cards at Alex, including the Wild, to get the most votes while keeping my 12s.

Drew.note: Casey is my best Meowfia suspect because of the shifting claims. I'll throw at Casey with two low cards to make the vote count, keeping my high cards.

Ellis.note: Casey is the most likely Meowfia partner, given the shifting Turkey, Tit and Hawk claims, so I won't throw at Casey. Drew is a steady Farm Eagle pushing the throw, so I'll throw a low card at Drew.

Finley.note: I'm dead, so my throw doesn't count as a vote, but it still scores. I'll throw my Wild, which is worth 0 if banked, at Casey, my suspect.

Alex.confusing: The Owl and Eagle rules were confusing, since several players misstated what those animals learn and whether an egg is gained for visitors. Nobody could tell which report was accurate until the reveal.
Alex.fun: Round 3 was the most fun: as Meowfia I baited Casey and Finley into fighting over who was the Turkey, then threw my whole nest at Casey for a 37-point round.
Alex.change: I would make the vote and egg-count reports more transparent so Farm players can cross-check claims. Right now a single wrong claim can swing a whole round.
Alex.regret: In rounds 1 and 2 I joined the pile-on against Ellis and Blair, who were both Farm, and threw away my cards. I would have asked for checkable evidence before throwing, instead of following whoever sounded most confident.

Blair.confusing: The Owl's rule was confusing at the table: "visited them" was read differently by different players, and it caused a lot of false accusations against Ellis in round 1. Several of us also couldn't tell how many eggs an Eagle should gain.
Blair.fun: Round 1 was a strong moment: as the Mouser, I got to play a Meowfia team and our throw on Ellis carried the vote, which banked 32 points for me. Watching the table build a case against Ellis from contradictory Owl stories was also fun.
Blair.change: I'd make the dawn egg reports and Eagle or Owl effects clearer, so every player reads the same count from the same rule. That would cut down on the false accusations and the confusion over whose story was right.
Blair.regret: In round 2 I wrongly "corrected" my own Eagle count and muddied my story, which gave the table a reason to vote on me. Knowing that Ellis was actually the Falcon, I'd have stated my real dawn report plainly from the start and not changed it.

Casey.confusing: The Owl's rule ("learns of all animals that visited THEM, the target") tripped up almost everyone, including Ellis, who explained it wrong twice. Eagle and Turkey egg counts were also hard to check against claims.
Casey.fun: Round 1, when I was Meowfia as the Sphinx and my Owl-result claim got picked apart by the table, and we still won the throw on Ellis. Watching the table argue over Turkey claims in Round 3 was also entertaining.
Casey.change: Make role claims harder to fake, like showing each player's animal as a public card or limiting duplicate roles, so two players can't both claim the same Turkey.
Casey.regret: In Round 3 I threw three cards at Alex on a Turkey-claim accusation, when I was Farm and should have kept more high cards; I'd instead have asked for Alex's visit details before committing so I didn't throw my 10s and 12s.

Drew.confusing: The Owl and Eagle wording caused the most trouble: I wrongly argued that an Owl learns who visited its target, and Blair's Eagle egg count was hard to pin down. Two players also both claimed Turkey in round 3, which I couldn't resolve.
Drew.fun: Round 2, when I was Meowfia with a Wink and the table spent the day arguing over Blair's Eagle count while I quietly steered the vote.
Drew.change: Show each player's visitors publicly at dawn, or at least the visit list for any target, so the Owl, Eagle, and Falcon claims can be checked directly instead of argued from memory.
Drew.regret: In round 3 I backed Casey's throw and trusted Alex's Turkey claim, but Alex was the Meowfia Sphinx and Casey was the real Turkey. I should have thrown at Alex instead of Casey.

Ellis.confusing: The Owl and Eagle wording was easy to misread, since the Owl learns visitors to its target, not to itself, and several of us, including me at first, got that wrong during the day. Eggsecution counts were also hard to track when some players were dead.
Ellis.fun: Round 2 was the most fun, with the Falcon, Eagle and Owl stories all colliding and the table arguing over who was lying about their egg changes.
Ellis.change: I would make the day's claims easier to check by having the Storyteller state which visitors each target had, so nobody can misremember how an egg change was produced.
Ellis.regret: In round 2 I helped push the vote against Blair over an Eagle count mismatch, and I should have kept my Falcon visit to myself and tested the claims instead of calling CAW. I would have held my throw until someone checked Drew's and Finley's stories.

Finley.confusing: The Owl card's "them" wording was ambiguous. I misread it, pushed a wrong accusation at Ellis, and had to retract it.
Finley.fun: As the Sphinx in round 2, I learned Alex was the Hawk, which made me a Meowfia player who knew a real Farm role. Our side then won the round with Blair's elimination.
Finley.change: I would make the Owl and Eagle card text more explicit about whose visitors they see. I would also reduce how easily a Wink can kill a player mid-vote.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I sided against Casey, who was a real Farm Turkey, and never tested Alex, who was the Meowfia Sphinx. I would have questioned Alex's Turkey claim directly instead of pushing Casey.
